Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

spatialGE 2.0.0

Behavior changes

  • transform_data() now populates vst.variance.standardized in @gene_meta. Previously the column was added only as a side effect of whichever analysis ran first, so whether get_gene_meta() showed it depended on call order, and gene_interpolation()/STplot_interpolation() dropped any existing column and recomputed it. transform_data() now computes it for both method='log' and method='sct', through the same calculate_vst() helper STclust() uses, so every caller sees one definition. Code that inspected colnames(get_gene_meta(x)) will see one additional column, and code that counted on STclust() being what created it no longer needs to.

    Note this does not change which genes any function selects: STclust(), STgradient(), gene_interpolation() and STdiff() already computed VST themselves before ranking, so their topgenes choices were consistent before this change too. (An earlier draft of this entry claimed otherwise, and also cited a top-20 overlap between gene_stdevs and VST rankings of 6; measured across the eight Visium samples of the tnbc_bassiouni set it is 7-13.) What changed is where the column comes from, not what downstream functions do with it.

    It does change column order, which matters if you index by position. Because transform_data() now adds the column before SThet() appends its statistics, get_gene_meta() returns

    1.2.2:  sample, gene, gene_mean, gene_stdevs, moran_i, geary_c, vst.variance.standardized
2.0.0:  sample, gene, gene_mean, gene_stdevs, vst.variance.standardized, moran_i, geary_c

    The same seven columns with the same contents, in a different order: VST used to arrive last, appended by whichever analysis ran first, and now sits ahead of moran_i/geary_c. Code selecting by name is unaffected; code using [[5]], [, 5:7] or tail(colnames(...), 1) will pick a different column. Select by name.

  • transform_data() no longer fails on a sample with very few variable genes. Because of the change above, transform_data() began fitting the variance-mean loess that vst.variance.standardized requires. That fit needs at least 4 genes with non-zero variance, and below it stats::loess stops with span is too small – so normalizing a very small or low-complexity STlist aborted, where in 1.2.2 it had succeeded. The count that matters is of non-constant genes, so a matrix with many genes of which only a few vary hit it as well. Such a sample now gets a warning naming it, and is left without the column rather than failing; calculate_vst() only computes when the column is absent, so a later analysis retries instead of inheriting a wrong value. Functions that rank genes by variability still raise an error on such a sample, since there is no ranking to return.

  • dim() on an STlist now obeys the base R contract. It returns c(n_genes, n_spots) as an integer vector when the object holds exactly one sample, and NULL for a multi-sample object – because there is no single gene x spot shape to report. It previously returned a named list of per-sample dimensions, which made nrow() and ncol() meaningless on an STlist and was reported by R CMD check as “dim() returns class ‘list’”. Use summarize_STlist() for a per-sample table of dimensions. Nothing inside the package called dim() on an STlist.

  • STlist objects are now validated at construction. setValidity() rejects a malformed object up front: a sample-keyed slot referring to a sample that is not in @counts, a count matrix without gene/spot names, or an @spatial_meta entry whose row count disagrees with the number of spots. These previously surfaced much later, far from their cause.

  • filter_data() reports what it did. Every count threshold defaults to 0 (and the *_max* thresholds to NULL), so a call supplying none of them filtered nothing – while looking like a successful filter. With the new verbose=TRUE default it now says explicitly that nothing was filtered, or how many samples, spots/cells and genes were removed. filter_data() remains single-threaded and deliberately has no cores argument, unlike the analysis functions.

  • Requesting a gene, annotation or reference domain that does not exist is now an error rather than a silent no-op. SThet(genes=), STgradient(annot=), STgradient(ref=) and gene_interpolation(genes=) previously accepted a name matching nothing and returned without complaint, so a typo looked like a run that legitimately found nothing. The rule is now: error when nothing matches, and message naming what was dropped when only some does. Code that relied on the no-op will now stop; that reliance was almost certainly accidental.

  • STenrich() now requires annot and domain together. Domain-restricted mode was guarded by !is.null(annot) & !is.null(domain), so supplying one without the other skipped the entire block: the unrestricted analysis ran and returned results a caller would reasonably read as domain-restricted, with nothing downstream able to detect the discrepancy. Supplying one alone is now an error. If you have results from 1.2.x produced by passing annot without domain, they are not domain-restricted and are worth regenerating.

  • SThet()’s default (k=NULL) statistics moved by ~2e-15. The distance-weighted complete graph is no longer materialized as a listw; Moran’s I and Geary’s C are computed directly from the coordinates in C++. Szero is bit-identical, and the residual difference is summation order inside the weighted dot product – four orders of magnitude below the ~2e-2 spot-order sensitivity already documented for SThet(k=). The reason for the change is capacity: the old listw needed 1.2 GB for a single 4,096-spot sample and about 181 GB extrapolated to 50,000 cells, i.e. it could not run on Xenium or CosMx data at all. It now completes in ~39 s using ~100 KB. @misc$sthet$listws is no longer populated on this path; SThet(k=) still builds a real spdep object.

  • gene_stdevs in @gene_meta moved by ~1e-16. Per-gene standard deviations are computed without densifying the matrix, which changes the summation order. Nothing downstream consumes gene_stdevs – topgenes selection uses vst.variance.standardized – and cluster assignments, all vst.* columns and @tr_counts were verified bit-identical.

  • A Seurat object’s platform is no longer assumed to be Visium. STlist() hardcoded @misc$platform = 'visium' for any Seurat input; it is now inferred from the image class. This matters because platform selects STgradient()’s default nb_dist_thr and branches in plot_image() and STplot_interpolation(), so importing an imaging-based (Xenium/CosMx) Seurat object previously produced results computed with Visium-appropriate distance thresholds.

  • pseudobulk_heatmap() displays a different set of genes, because it was selecting the wrong ones. The heatmap keeps the hm_display_genes most variable genes, ranked by coefficient of variation, but the CV was computed upside down as mean/sd instead of sd/mean. Sorting that decreasing put the highest mean/sd first – that is, the lowest true CV – so the plot showed the most uniformly-expressed genes rather than the most variable ones, the exact opposite of the intent. Any heatmap produced by 1.2.x is showing the wrong gene set and is worth regenerating.

  • cores= is now honored by STlist() and transform_data(). Both accepted the argument and then ignored it, so they always ran at the auto-detected core count no matter what was passed. Passing cores= now actually changes the number of forked workers. Two consequences: wall-clock times for these two functions will differ from 1.2.x for any explicit cores=, and because forked children re-seed their own RNG, transform_data(method='sct') is only reproducible at cores=1 once a sample exceeds sctransform::vst’s internal sampling threshold. Pass cores=1 where exact SCT reproducibility matters.

  • Spot/cell ordering within an STlist is now deterministic. process_lists() contained a coordinate sort that silently had no effect, so through 1.2.2 spots simply retained whatever order they appeared in in the input files – meaning two files describing the same tissue with rows in a different order produced differently-ordered STlists. The sort now applies, so ordering depends on the coordinates themselves rather than on input file layout.

    Note what it sorts by: the third column of the coordinate data, whichever that is, not xpos specifically. With the usual libname, ypos, xpos column order that means xpos, and because the sort is stable the result reads as xpos then ypos. Supply the coordinate columns in a different order and the sort key changes with them.

    No function signatures, arguments, or return types changed. Counts, transformed counts, and the vst.* gene-level statistics are bit-identical once matched by name. What changes for them is order: the column order of @counts/@tr_counts, the row order of @spatial_meta, and therefore the row order of results built from them. Code that addresses spots by libname is unaffected; code that indexes them positionally, or that depends on how ties break in an adj_p_value-sorted result, may need updating.

    Four results are not merely reordered, because they depend on spot order by construction rather than by layout. All four behaved this way in 1.2.x too – there, the order came from your input file, so the same tissue supplied with rows in a different order gave different numbers. Ordering is now determined by the coordinates, which removes that file-layout dependence, but the underlying sensitivity remains and is worth knowing about:

    • STenrich() p-values. The permutation null is drawn over spot positions, so a fixed seed selects a different random subset when the spots are in a different order. The observed statistic is unaffected; only the null, and therefore p_value/adj_p_value, move.
    • SThet(k = ) Moran’s I. With k given, neighbours come from a k-nearest neighbour graph, and on a regular grid the k-th distance is tied between several spots; the tie is broken by position. On our test data Moran’s I moves by up to 0.02 – large enough to matter. SThet() without k uses a distance-based weight list and is unaffected (agreement to ~1e-15).
    • STgradient(distsumm = 'avg') Spearman correlations. Averaging each spot’s distances to the reference domain produces exact ties on a regular grid, and a change in summation order of ~1e-16 is enough to flip one, which flips a rank. Correlations move by up to 0.004. distsumm = 'min' does not create the same ties.
    • plot_counts() density curves, which plot a seeded random distrib_subset of spots selected by position. Cosmetic, but the curve is not identical. The point jitter in distribution_plots(plot_type = 'violin') behaves the same way.

    If you need a value that does not depend on spot order at all, prefer SThet() without k and STgradient(distsumm = 'min'), and raise reps in STenrich() so the permutation estimate is less sensitive to which subset is drawn.

New features

  • An STlist can now be subset by sample, and has a length. x[i] returns a new, valid STlist holding only the selected spatial arrays, and length(x) reports how many it holds. Previously neither worked: subsetting failed with “object of type ‘S4’ is not subsettable”, and length(x) returned the number of slots (7) rather than samples, so seq_along(x) and for(i in seq_len(length(x))) silently did the wrong thing. To work with one sample out of a multi-sample object you had to rebuild an STlist from the raw files.

    Select by name (x[tissue_names(x)[1]]), position, negative position or logical vector. Every sample-keyed slot is subset alongside @counts – @spatial_meta, @gene_meta, @tr_counts, and the per-sample level inside each @gene_krige element – so the result passes validity, and @sample_meta rows are matched to their sample rather than sliced positionally. Subsetting is deliberately one-dimensional: an STlist holds several arrays with independent gene and spot sets, so there is no shared second dimension. x[i, j] and x[[i]] raise an error saying so. An unknown sample name is also an error, listing the available names, rather than a silent omission.

  • Parallelism on Windows. resolve_cores() returned 1L unconditionally on Windows and sge_lapply() forwarded only to parallel::mclapply, which has no fork() there – so the package was entirely serial. A non-forking (PSOCK) backend is now used on Windows, and can be forced anywhere with options(spatialGE.psock=TRUE). mclapply remains the default where fork() exists. The spatialGE.cores/SPATIALGE_CORES override is also now consulted before any platform decision; it was previously ignored on Windows.

  • Seurat v5 support, and conversion in both directions. Seurat input was v4 only: v5 stores counts in an Assay5’s layers, so the old access returned NULL, and v5’s VisiumV2/FOV images carry no @coordinates frame. Both are handled now, the assay defaults to DefaultAssay() rather than a hardcoded 'Spatial', and the import is sparse-to-sparse instead of densifying every gene by every cell across all slices up front. as_Seurat() is new and provides the reverse conversion.

  • Optional on-disk storage. STlist_to_disk(x, root) moves count matrices into per-sample parquet files so data larger than memory can be held and read in gene-subset slices; STlist_to_memory() reverses it, exactly. Opt-in and off by default – an STlist built the normal way is unchanged. is_backed() and validate_store() support it. Note this buys capacity, not speed: aggregates still compute in memory, so a backed STlist is currently slower on those paths.

  • Large-data performance. Several operations no longer densify sparse matrices. Measured on a 200-gene x 50,000-cell synthetic sample: filter_data() 27x faster, per-gene standard deviations 42x, and log transformation 33x (bit-identical output).

  • STgradient()’s distance step no longer materializes the n x n distance matrix. stgradient_dists_one_sample() built as.matrix(stats::dist(coords)) – 934 MB allocated at 4,096 spots and about 20 GB at 50,000 cells, so the function could not run on Xenium or CosMx data at all. The distances are now computed in C++ in O(n) memory. Output is bit-identical for both distsumm='min' and distsumm='avg' (the latter reproduces R’s two-pass corrected mean()), so no results change; measured 1.6x faster and about 3,100x less allocation at 4,096 spots, and 50,000 cells now completes instead of failing to allocate.

  • STdiff()’s t_test and wilcoxon paths are 17-27x faster. stdiff_mean_test() re-filtered and re-selected the whole expression frame once per gene x cluster combination; the two groups depend only on the annotation, so the split is now computed with base indexing and the gene column is pulled directly. Output is unchanged – the same t.test/wilcox.test calls on the same vectors. The default mm path is not affected.

  • Set the environment variable SPATIALGE_CORES, or the option spatialGE.cores, to force every parallelized call site to run serially and in-process without editing any code. Intended for profiling (profvis cannot see inside parallel::mclapply’s forks) and for debugging a worker that fails only under forking. The option takes precedence over the environment variable. This is a development aid and is deliberately not part of the documented API.

Bug fixes

  • STlist validity no longer rejects an object that has kriging results. setValidity() treated @gene_krige as sample-keyed and compared its names to the sample names, but that slot is keyed by gene first and sample second (x@gene_krige[[gene]][[sample]]), so its top-level names are gene symbols. Every object returned by gene_interpolation() was therefore reported invalid – but only when validity actually ran, and assignment through @<- does not trigger it, so the function appeared to succeed and a later validObject() (or any construction from that object) failed. The sample level is now checked, one gene at a time.

  • load_images() no longer drops samples whose image is not the first path match. Two defects combined: sample-to-file matching used a vectorized & where it needed a scalar &&, and the match was positional, so with more than one image directory or a sample whose name did not sort first the wrong file – or no file – was attached. Matching is now by normalized sample name, across every supplied directory and both extensions (.png/.jpg/.jpeg), with a decoder fallback when the file extension disagrees with its actual encoding. A sample whose image genuinely cannot be read is skipped with a warning rather than silently, and if no image matches at all the error names what was searched.

  • STplot_interpolation() works on its documented default. With the default genes=NULL it selected genes by VST but then intersected that selection with a kriging-derived gene list; because it also required the column to be present, the call failed on any STlist that had not already been through gene_interpolation(). It now errors with a clear message when the object has no kriged genes, restricts to those that do exist (warning only when the user named genes explicitly), uses calculate_vst() rather than its own inline copy, and errors clearly when a color scale has no finite values.

  • STdiff() explains an unusable annot= instead of failing inside dplyr. A numeric metadata column – a perfectly ordinary one, such as total_counts – reached an internal join and produced Can't join `x$orig_annot` with `y$orig_annot` due to incompatible types. i `x$orig_annot` is a <double>, which names neither the function nor the argument to change. annot must hold group labels, so a numeric column now raises an error naming STdiff, the requirement and the fix (as.character()), as does a column with fewer than two distinct groups – which previously produced no usable comparison.

  • transform_data(method='sct') reports an actionable error when SCTransform fails. On a small or low-complexity matrix sctransform::vst() failed with missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed, giving no indication of which sample, how large it was, or what to change. The error now names the sample and its dimensions (n_genes x spots/cells) and suggests lowering sct_n_regr_genes or using method='log', while still reporting the underlying message.

  • A bad cores= value is caught on every parallelized path. The gene-metadata step of transform_data() never validated it, so cores='abc' coerced to NA and was handed directly to the parallel lapply instead of raising an error. Validation is now centralized (see Minor), which fixes that path and removes the five duplicated checks elsewhere.

  • pseudobulk_samples() no longer fails on a gene whose pseudobulk total is constant across samples. Such a gene produced an all-NaN column after scaling and prcomp() rejected it outright, so any dataset containing an all-zero gene – routine after a permissive filter_data() – could not be analysed. Those genes are now dropped with a warning.

  • SThet() no longer fails when @spatial_meta has been row-subset with base [. Both spatial-weight builders fed the frame to tibble::column_to_rownames(), which rejects non-contiguous row names, so the call died with an error naming neither SThet nor the cause. This is the same defect that made STenrich()’s domain= path unreachable through 1.2.2, in two call sites that fix did not cover.

  • STenrich() no longer crashes on a gene set with exactly one gene present. Subsetting dropped the matrix to a dimensionless vector, which DelayedMatrixStats::colMeans2() rejects – even though min_genes=1 explicitly permits single-gene sets.

  • Seurat_FindVariableFeatures() no longer fails on any input that is not already a dgCMatrix. It called as.sparse(), which is SeuratObject::as.sparse() and was never imported, so the call had been unresolvable since the code was vendored – masked because every caller happened to pass a dgCMatrix, and because the name was listed in utils::globalVariables(), suppressing the check NOTE that would have caught it.

  • STlist() accepts a Seurat object with samples=NULL. The sample-name parsing tested an argument derived from samples before reaching the Seurat branch, so the normal way to call it raised “argument is of length zero”.

  • filter_data() can now produce a sample with exactly one surviving spot. The dense intermediate collapsed to a vector at one column, which then broke row-name handling.

  • transform_data(), SThet(), STenrich() and gene_interpolation() report invalid input as spatialGE errors naming the function and argument, instead of surfacing internal failures such as object 'tr_results' not found or attempt to select less than one element in get1index.

  • STenrich(annot=, domain=) now works. Domain-restricted gene set testing was announced in 1.2.1 but never functioned: restricting to a domain subsets the spatial metadata rows, which leaves stray row names that tibble::column_to_rownames() rejects, so the call always failed with ​`.data` must be a data frame without row names. Every domain-restricted call in 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 errored out. The unrestricted and score_type='gsva' paths were unaffected.

  • All 14 documented function examples now run. A doubled roxygen comment marker (#' #' zip_tmp = ...) commented out the assignment that the following unzip() call depended on, so every example failed with object 'zip_tmp' not found. Each example’s tryCatch reported this as “Could not run example. Are you connected to the internet?”, misattributing a code defect to the network, while R CMD check still reported checking examples ... OK.

  • STgradient() no longer leaks state between genes. pval_warn was only assigned inside a branch that requires more than one spot in the fitted range, so a gene that fell below that threshold left the previous gene’s value in place. Affects the pval_comment column only.

  • .github/ is no longer shipped inside the package tarball (added to .Rbuildignore).

Minor

  • User-facing validation errors are now raised through the shared error catalog, so they all carry the spatialGE exception: signature. About thirty sites used a bare stop(), which meant an argument-validation failure looked no different from an internal crash; and three sites wrote the spatialGE exception: prefix by hand instead of using the catalog, so their wording could drift from it. Their text is unchanged in substance but now lives in inst/err.csv, and raise_err() gained optional sprintf-style interpolation so messages that embed a gene name, sample size or threshold can be catalogued too. Code matching on the exact wording of these messages may need updating; matching on spatialGE exception: (the documented pattern) is unaffected.

  • An unusable cores= value now fails the same way everywhere. Validation of a core count used to be each call site’s job, and was done three different ways: some sites raised error0032, others error0036, five used an uncatalogued bare stop(), and transform_data()’s gene-metadata path did not check at all – so cores='abc' there became NA and was passed straight into the parallel lapply. Resolution now happens once in resolve_cores(), which rejects a value that is not one finite positive number with an error naming the fix. The caller’s coercion is preserved: coerce='ceiling' and coerce='none' still return a non-integral value unchanged.

  • The error raised when an argument that should be an STlist is NULL or of the wrong type now reads cannot get a slot (...) from an object of type ... rather than no applicable method for `@` applied to an object of class ..., because the shared argument-resolution helper reads slots via methods::slot(). Both messages are raw R errors and neither is informative; nothing is caught or handled differently.

  • STdiff() no longer emits dplyr’s “Detected an unexpected many-to-many relationship” warning under dplyr 1.1 and later. The gene x annotation table it builds is deliberately many-to-many – every gene of a sample combines with every annotation of that sample – but it was declared with the deprecated multiple='all', which newer dplyr checks separately from relationship= and therefore ignores. The join now declares relationship='many-to-many'. The joined rows, and every result built from them, are unchanged.

spatialGE 1.2.22025-06-04

spatialGE 1.2.12025-05-26

  • Added C++ code to speed up STenrich computations (Thank you, Dr. Soupir!).
  • The STenrich function can now calculate gene set enrichment scores (via GSVA) in addition to gene set average expression.
  • The STenrich function can now test for gene set “hot-spots” within an specific tissue domain (annot and domain arguments).
  • Spatial distances can now be log-transformed for STgradient (log argument).
  • Example data sets are now in the spatialGE_Data GitHub repository.
  • New functions spatial_metadata and tissue_names to quickly access the names of spot/cell annotations and sample names.
  • Re-assessed package dependencies.
  • Use of DelayedArray for some calculations.
  • Several bug fixes.

spatialGE 1.2.02025-05-13

  • Functions STenrich, STgradient, and STdiff available.
  • Added C++ code for Seurat’s implementation of FindVariableFeatures

spatialGE 1.1.0

  • Multiple, significant changes to STlist (incompatible with STlist objects from version 1.0).
